sections.title: Introduction
rules: High-dimensional data increases storage costs, computational runtime, and model variance.
The curse of dimensionality makes data sparse in high-dimensional spaces.
Dimensionality reduction maps data from d dimensions to a lower dimension k.
Feature selection chooses a subset of the original features.
Feature extraction creates new combinations of the original features.
Reducing dimensionality improves learning speed, prevents overfitting, and enables visual data exploration.

sections.title: Subset Selection
rules: Subset selection finds the best subset of k features out of d original features.
Evaluating all two to the power of d subsets is computationally infeasible.
Forward feature selection starts with an empty set and greedily adds the most useful feature.
Backward feature selection starts with all features and greedily removes the least useful feature.
Filter methods rank features using statistical tests independent of the machine learning model.
Wrapper methods evaluate feature subsets using the classification accuracy of a specific learning algorithm.

sections.title: Principal Components Analysis
rules: Principal Components Analysis is an unsupervised linear dimensionality reduction method.
PCA finds orthogonal projection axes that maximize the variance of projected data.
Maximizing projected variance is equivalent to minimizing reconstruction error.
The first principal component is the eigenvector of the covariance matrix with the largest eigenvalue.
Each subsequent principal component is an orthogonal eigenvector with the next largest eigenvalue.
The eigenvalues quantify the variance captured along each principal axis.
We choose k components to capture a desired proportion of the total data variance.
Standardizing input features is necessary when features have different measurement scales.

sections.title: Factor Analysis
rules: Factor analysis assumes observed variables depend linearly on a small number of unobserved latent factors.
Latent factors represent shared underlying causes that generate correlations among observed features.
The factor loadings matrix specifies the contribution of each latent factor to observed variables.
Factor analysis explicitly separates common variance from unique variable-specific noise.
Unlike PCA, factor analysis assumes a generative statistical model for observed data.
Factor rotation rotates the factor axes to make loadings easier to interpret.

sections.title: Multidimensional Scaling
rules: Multidimensional scaling maps high-dimensional points into two or three dimensions while preserving pairwise distances.
The input to multidimensional scaling is an N by N matrix of pairwise distances.
Classical multidimensional scaling uses double centering to convert the distance matrix into an inner product matrix.
The algorithm calculates low-dimensional coordinates from the top eigenvectors of the inner product matrix.
Non-metric multidimensional scaling preserves the rank order of distances using a stress objective function.

sections.title: Linear Discriminant Analysis
rules: Linear Discriminant Analysis is a supervised linear dimensionality reduction method.
LDA finds projection directions that maximize separation between class means.
LDA simultaneously minimizes the variance within each individual class.
The within-class scatter matrix measures the spread of instances around their class means.
The between-class scatter matrix measures the spread of class means around the overall mean.
Fisher's linear discriminant maximizes the ratio of between-class scatter to within-class scatter.
For K classes, LDA projects data into at most K minus one dimensions.

sections.title: Isomap
rules: Euclidean distance fails when high-dimensional data lies on a curved non-linear manifold.
Isomap is a non-linear dimensionality reduction algorithm based on geodesic distances.
The algorithm first builds a neighborhood graph connecting each point to its k-nearest neighbors.
Isomap calculates shortest path lengths between all node pairs on the graph using Dijkstra's algorithm.
The shortest graph paths approximate true geodesic distances across the curved manifold surface.
Classical multidimensional scaling then embeds the geodesic distance matrix into low-dimensional Euclidean space.

sections.title: Locally Linear Embedding
rules: Locally Linear Embedding is an unsupervised non-linear manifold learning algorithm.
LLE preserves local neighborhood relationships without estimating global pairwise distances.
In the first step, LLE finds the k-nearest neighbors for each data point.
In the second step, LLE computes weights that reconstruct each point as a linear combination of its neighbors.
The reconstruction weights are invariant to rotation, translation, and scaling.
In the third step, LLE computes low-dimensional coordinates that preserve these linear reconstruction weights.
Solving the third step reduces to finding the bottom eigenvectors of a sparse matrix.

sections.title: Notes
rules: Karl Pearson invented Principal Components Analysis in nineteen zero-one.
Ronald Fisher developed Linear Discriminant Analysis in nineteen thirty-six.
Joshua Tenenbaum and colleagues introduced Isomap in two thousand.
Sam Roweis and Lawrence Saul introduced Locally Linear Embedding in two thousand.
